what_its_for: Flurbiprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis (such as rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis). The eye drop form (Ocufen) is used before eye surgery to prevent the pupil from getting smaller during the procedure.
how_to_take: Take flurbiprofen tablets by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take it with food, milk, or antacids to help prevent stomach upset. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking it. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. If using the eye drop form, wash your hands before use, tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place the drops inside. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and avoid blinking. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye or any surface.
dosing: For adults with arthritis, the usual dose is 200 to 300 mg per day, divided into 2 to 4 smaller doses (for example, 50 mg four times a day or 100 mg twice a day). The maximum dose is 300 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not take more than prescribed. For the eye drop form, your doctor or surgical team will administer the drops before your eye procedure.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store flurbiprofen tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking flurbiprofen, as it increases your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen, naproxen, or aspirin) at the same time unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid lying down right after taking the tablet. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if this medication makes you feel dizzy or drowsy. Avoid prolonged sun exposure, as flurbiprofen may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: stomach pain, black or tarry stools, or vomiting blood (signs of stomach bleeding); chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, or slurred speech (signs of a heart attack or stroke); swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); skin rash, blistering, or peeling; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual weight gain or swelling in your legs or ankles; changes in urination or signs of kidney problems; or severe headache or vision changes. Seek emergency help (call 911) immediately if you think you are having a serious reaction.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some pain relief within the first few hours of taking flurbiprofen. However, the full anti-inflammatory benefit for arthritis symptoms — such as reduced swelling and stiffness — may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of flurbiprofen, especially stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and fluid retention. Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Pregnancy: Do not use flurbiprofen during the last 3 months of pregnancy (third trimester) as it can harm the unborn baby, especially the baby's heart and kidneys. Talk to your doctor before using it during the first or second trimester. Breastfeeding: Flurbiprofen may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established. Use only if directed by a pediatric doctor. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to monitor you closely or adjust your dose.
